aboleth_brain.name: Aboleth Brain
aboleth_brain.desc:
*The Brain of a young Aboleth, tainted by an otherwordly power.* The brain can be consumed, granting the following bonuses:

***Otherwordly Memories***
Your mind becomes flooded with cosmic memories that aren't your own. Once per day, you may attempt to call upon these memories to try and glean some information about a particular item, place, creature or course of action by making a Wisdom saving throw.

On a **20+**, you may ask the DM one question, and receive a vague but truthful answer, provided the answer is within these memories. If it is not, the daily use of this feature is not consumed.

On a **15-19**, you may ask the DM one question, and receive a vision associated with the question asked, provided the answer is within these memories.

On a **14** or lower, you take 3d8 psychic damage and have the stunned condition for 1 minute, as your mind is flooded with incomprehensible thoughts.

***Improved Mutations***
You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with your organic weapons.

***Devouring Urge***
Once per turn when you hit a creature with your organic weapon, you can deal an extra 1d6 Necrotic or Psychic damage (your choice) to the creature, and you can expend one of your Hit Point Dice to roll it and regain a number of Hit Points equal to the roll plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 Hit Point). You can only use this feature once per turn. In addition, the flesh consumed by the creature temporarily alters your form. The DM will either:

- *Grant you a temporary mutation of the DM's choice, which last for 1 minute. Using this feature again on a different creature will replace an existing mutation with the newest one.*

- *Roll a d100. You gain a random mutation from the Mutations Table, which lasts for 1 minute. Using this feature again on a different creature will replace any existing mutation/s with the newest one/s.*

amulet_of_the_watcher.name: Amulet of the Watcher
amulet_of_the_watcher.desc:
Gain +1 to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your spells.
Gain proficiency in perception. If you already have proficiency, gain expertise instead.

Additionally, as an action, you can place up to two spectral eyes (only visible with a DC20 Perception or DC15 Arcana check) firmly on a solid surface—such as a wall, table, or boot—where it remains until destroyed. While you're within 5 feet of an eye, you can use a bonus action to speak the command word to cause its eye to open. The opening is about the size of a keyhole, and by peering through it, you can open and see through another eye's opening of your choice. You choose which eye to look through the first time you peer into the hole and can change it again using a bonus action. If another eye is placed when two are already active, the eye that was placed *first* disappears in a non-harmful yet visible & audible explosion of blue light.

The eyes you can choose to see through in this way must be a part of the set, be placed on a solid surface, and be on the same plane of existence as the one you're looking through. You can only see through one eye at a time, which operates both ways, and nothing can pass through the hole. If another eye attempts to look through one you're already using, the connection between the first two ends and is replaced by the new one. An eye closes when it's no longer being looked through.

Each eye has AC 10 and 5 hit points. If it drops to 0 hit points, the eye is destroyed. If a target or area is immune to divination magic or can't be perceived through scrying sensors, it doesn't appear through the hole.

Third Eye. When you make a Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check involving sight, you can roll 1d4 and add the number rolled to the ability check.

Primeval Awakening:
The Amulet has 10 charges, and regains 1d4 daily at Dawn. You can cast the following spells using the amulets charges:
Darkvision: 2 Charges
See Invisibility: 2 Charges
Arcane Eye: 5 Charges
True Seeing: 10 Charges
Eyebite: 10 Charges

abjurer_s_gilder.name: Abjurer's Gilder
abjurer_s_gilder.desc:
This golden badge is usually given to Wizards who either excel at or have mastered Abjuration magic as a symbol of their accomplishments. 

While wearing this badge, you always have the *Shield* spell prepared if it's in your spellbook, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can have prepared. 

In addition, when you are hit by an attack roll or targeted by the Magic Missile spell, you can take a special Reaction, instead of your normal one, to cast Shield. This special Reaction can be used before or after your normal Reaction for the round, but it can't be used on the same turn as your normal Reaction. 

Once you take this special Reaction you can't do so again until the start of your next turn.

eye_of_the_watcher.name: Eye of the Watcher
eye_of_the_watcher.desc:
While you are attuned to this item, you can cast *see invisibility* on yourself at will.

*Curse.* When you attune to the Eye of The Watcher, you are suddenly overcome with the urge to see what it sees. Make a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw. On a success, you're able to resist the enchantment and are aware of the curse's effects, but are not attuned to it. On a failure, you forcefully tear out one of your own Eyes, taking 4d10 necrotic damage, allowing the Eye of The Watcher to crawl into its place. If you are already missing an Eye, you are simply compelled to allow the Eye to crawl into the empty socket.

You can see normally while the Eye of The Watcher remains in your socket, but can choose to close your other Eye to see through its magically enhanced lens using a bonus action. Looking through the Eye grants you darkvision of up to 120 feet, and are able to peer through both magical and nonmagical darkness using it. The Eye moves slower than a normal Eye, leaving slight trails and motion blurs behind it as you look through it. While looking only through the Eye of The Watcher, you have disadvantage on any attack you make as well as ability checks that rely on depth perception. You can open your other Eye and regain your normal vision using another bonus action.

*The Watcher familiar.* The Eye is a gruesome familiar. As an action, you can command the Eye to crawl out of its socket and move independently of you. Use the abilities described in the *find familiar* spell when commanding the Eye of The Watcher. The Eye has five hit points, an AC of 12, a movement and climbing speed of 20 feet, does not require air to breathe, and has a +6 bonus to Dexterity (stealth) checks. If the Eye is slain or you dismiss it, it reappears inside your open Eye socket with a sickly sound. If it was slain, you cannot use its magical sight or command it as a familiar again until the following dusk.

Targeting the Eye with the *remove curse* spell or unattuning to it causes the Eye to pull itself out of the socket and crawl away. Slaying the Eye while it is unattuned to a creature destroys the item.

*The dark Eye swiveled, slightly. It was inhuman, to say the least, but its secrets were too vast to discredit.*

Eye Crawler - Tiny Aberration, Chaotic Neutral. 
Armor Class 12. 
Hit Points 2 (1d4). 
Speed 30 ft., Climb 30 ft. 
Initiative +1 (11). 

STR 3 (-4), 
DEX 13 (+1), 
CON 10 (+0), 
INT 6 (-2), 
WIS 11 (+0), 
CHA 5 (-3). 

Skills Stealth +6. 
Senses Darkvision 120 ft.

blade_of_the_chosen.name: Blade of the Chosen
blade_of_the_chosen.desc:
A Magical Weapon said to have been forged by Druenol himself, that has been bestowed upon only the greatest warriors for generations, destined by fate. After attuning to the weapon, the weapon shifts into a Melee Simple or Martial weapon of the user's choice, and cannot change after attuning to the user.

You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The weapon has 7 runes inscribed into it.
In Darkness, the unsheathed weapon sheds moonlight, creating Bright Light in a 15-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 15 feet.

Rune 1: Fey Step
As a Bonus Action - You or a Willing Creature you touch can teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 30ft. You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per dawn.
Rune 2: Dormant
Rune 3: Dormant
Rune 4: Dormant
Rune 5: Dormant
Rune 6: Dormant
Rune 7: Dormant

grantedResources.name: Rune 1 - Fey Step
grantedResources.desc:
As a Bonus Action - You or a Willing Creature you touch can teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 30ft.

Prof bonus times per dawn.

ring_of_the_cosmos.name: Ring of the Cosmos
ring_of_the_cosmos.desc:
Looking into the main gemstone of this ring shows the landscape of one of the Planes, which changes daily. To determine the plane, roll 1d8 at dusk (provided you are on the Material Plane) and consult the table below. (Note, if you are on any of the planes listed, the ring automatically shows a landscape from the plane you are present on).

| 1d8 | Plane | Creature Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Astral Sea | Aberration |
| 2 | Shadowfell | Undead |
| 3 | Feywild | Fey |
| 4 | The 9 Hells | Fiend |
| 5 | The Triad of the Heavens | Celestial |
| 6 | The Eternal Forge | Construct |
| 7 | Mount Vertaei | Humanoid, Giant |
| 8 | Elemental Planes | Elemental |

1/Dawn, you can use a *magic action* to transform into a creature of the type listed next to the plane of CR less than or equal to your level divided by 3 (round down). When you do this, you retain your Hit Points, Hit Dice, proficiencies, personality, and ability to communicate. Your alignment also stays the same, but is influenced somewhat by the creature you transform into, finding yourself occasionally wanting to do similar things to the chosen creature. You choose if you retain your mental stats (INT, WIS, CHA) or take the creatures.

You Do Not gain the creatures Legendary Resistances, Condition Immunities, Initiative Bonus or Regional Effects if there are any.

Upon shape-shifting, you determine whether your equipment drops to the ground or changes in size and shape to fit the new form while you're in it, with the exception of the ring, which will take shape either as a ring or an amulet- your choice. You retain this form until the next dawn, or until dismissed.

Cursed
Frequent use of this ring has effects on the users mind. At the DM's discretion after transforming into a powerful creature, the DM may make you roll 1d20 on the following table.

| 1d20 | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Broken Mind. You immediately transform into the chosen creature under the DM's control. Your soul leaves your body & becomes trapped within the ring, appearing in the planescapes within the gemstones. Only a Wish spell can remove someone trapped this way. |
| 2 | Planar Summoning. You summon the creature you are transformed in a space within 30ft of you, chosen by the DM. The creature is hostile to you and your allies, and your transformation fails. |
| 3 | Chaotic Infusion. Roll 1d100. The ring gains a Major detrimental property permanently. |
| 4 | Arcane Anomaly. Roll 1d100. Trigger an Arcane Anomaly centered on yourself. |
| 5 | Planar Destruction. A random magic item that you have in your inventory that isn't the Ring of the Cosmos disintegrates into dust. Artifacts are excluded. |
| 6 | Shattered Mind. You have the Stunned Condition for 1 minute. |
| 7 | Chaotic Infusion. Roll 1d100. The ring gains a Minor detrimental property permanently. |
| 8 | Magical Contagion. You have the Lichen Plague Magical Contagion. The Contagion cannot spread. |
| 9 | Magical Contagion. You have the The Rusting Magical Contagion. The Contagion cannot spread. |
| 10 | Cosmically Jinxed. Whenever you make an attack roll, ability check or saving throw, roll 2d4. Subtract the result from the check. |
| 11 | Dazed Mind. While transformed, you can only take an action or bonus action on your turn, not both. |
| 12 | Exhausted Mind. Gain 2 levels of Exhaustion. |
| 13 | Exhausted Mind. Gain 1 level of Exhaustion. |
| 14 | Exhausted Mind. Gain 1 level of Exhaustion. |
| 15 | Altered Mind. Your alignment is permanently changed to the alignment of the creature you have just transformed into. This can be undone by a Greater Restoration spell. |
| 16 | Addled Mind. While transformed, you have Disadvantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma attacks rolls, ability checks, and saving throws. |
| 17 | Planar Contamination. Gain 1 level of Contamination & automatically gain a mutation. |
| 18 | Planar Contamination. Gain 1 level of Contamination & automatically gain a mutation. |
| 19 | Chaotic Infusion. Roll 1d100. The ring gains a Minor Beneficial Property permanently. |
| 20 | Become Immune to the effects of this table for 7 days, and the ring regains its charge. |

magebane_bolas.name: Magebane Bolas
magebane_bolas.desc:
You can make a ranged weapon attack with these bolas against a Large or smaller creature. 

When you do, you throw the bolas at the target; on a hit, the target takes the *1d4 bludgeoning* damage, and it must succeed on a Strength saving throw (*DC = 8 + Dex + Prof*) or be knocked prone and entangled by the bolas. 

If the target has the ability to cast spells, they subtract *1d6* from this save and future saves made attempting to escape the bolas. While entangled in this way, the target's has the *restrained* condition, and is unable to speak. The target remains entangled until it's freed. 

A creature can use its action to make a *DC 12* Strength check, freeing itself or another creature within reach on a success. If the target has the *Spellcasting* or *Pact-Magic* feature, the *DC* becomes *18*.

ring_of_silence.name: Ring of Silence
ring_of_silence.desc: While wearing this ring, you cannot speak, utter sounds with your voice, or cast spells with verbal components.

ring_of_response.name: Ring of Response
ring_of_response.desc:
Second Response. If you've already used your reaction this round, you can spend 1 charge to take another reaction. It can't be used to cast a spell or to respond to the same trigger twice.

Spell Battery. As an action, a creature touching the ring can expend a spell slot to restore 1 charge per level of the slot. The ring holds a maximum of 3 charges.

crimson_moon_blade.name: Crimson Moon-Blade
crimson_moon_blade.desc:
The typical Crimson Moon-Blade, an uncommon item, rapier/longsword with curved metal guard that protects your hand. The sword has 7 charges and regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn.

The following Crimson Moon-Blade, is a very rare variant with more powerful properties. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. In addition, when you expend 1 of the weapon's charges when you hit with an attack, the light is crimson moonlight, and deals an extra 2d6 radiant damage to the target, instead of 1d6. If the target has the Sunlight Sensitivity or Sunlight Hypersensitivity trait, such as a drow or vampire, it's considered to be in sunlight until the end of its next turn.

the_king_in_yellow.name: The King in Yellow
the_king_in_yellow.desc:
A slim play-script bound in cloth the color of old fever, no author credited. Its first act is dull. No one has ever left its second act unread.

**Attunement.** You can't choose to end attunement to this book. It ends only if the book is destroyed. Attuning to this book doesn't count against the number of magic items you can be attuned to.

**Act I: The Stranger.** When you attune to this book, choose one of the following. You have no memory of how you came by it.
- _**Spell.**_ You learn one spell of your choice from any class's spell list. You always have it prepared, and you can cast it once without a spell slot, regaining this ability when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast it using any spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it (choose when you attune).
- _**Feat.**_ You gain one Origin feat of your choice.

**Spell Granted:** *Plant Growth*

**Act II: The Yellow Sign.** When you finish a Long Rest without having read Act II, make a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw, which increases by 1 for each success. On a failure, you've read it. Once you have, you bear *the Yellow Sign*, visible only to those who have read the play, and you gain the following properties.

_**Carcosa's Favor.**_ You have Advantage on saving throws against the Frightened condition, and you gain Proficiency and Expertise in Charisma (Performance).

_**I Wear No Mask.**_ As a Bonus Action, you gain Truesight out to 30 feet for 1 minute. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

_**Have You Found the Yellow Sign?**_ As a Magic action, you ask the question of one creature you can see within 60 feet that can hear you. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (your spell save DC, or DC 15 if you lack the Spellcasting feature) or have the Frightened and Incapacitated conditions until the end of its next turn, at which point it must repeat the save. If it fails the second save, it has the Unconscious condition for 1 minute. The effect ends on the target if it takes damage or someone within 5 feet of it takes an action to shake it free. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

_**An Audience with the King.**_ When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points, or in another moment of desperate struggle (DM's discretion), you can beg an audience with the King in Yellow (no action required). For an instant you stand in Carcosa, and the King grants you one of the following:
- **Rise.** You regain all your Hit Points, and all conditions on you end.
- **Unmask.** Each creature of your choice within 60 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (same DC as above) or have the Frightened condition for 1 minute, during which its Speed is 0. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
- **Command.** You immediately cast any spell of level 6 or lower without expending a spell slot or needing components.

**The King's Favour.** Roll on the Carcosan Madness table; the effect lasts until ended by *Greater Restoration* or *Remove Curse*. The King also asks a favor of you, chosen by the DM. You can't use this property again until you've granted it.

_**Curse: Carcosan Madness.**_ Whenever you finish a Long Rest, roll a d20. On a 1, roll on the Carcosan Madness table; the effect lasts until your next Long Rest. On a 20, you dream of twin suns and gain Heroic Inspiration.

| **d10** | Carcosan Madness                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| :-----: | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
|  **1**  | **Lost Carcosa.** Sometimes you forget which world is the real one. Whenever you roll Initiative, roll a d6. On a 1, you have the Incapacitated condition until the end of your first turn.                                                                                                                             |
|  **2**  | **The Black Stars.** You keep searching a sky that isn't there, even indoors. You have Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight, but you always know which way is north and how long it is until the next dawn or dusk.                                                                            |
|  **3**  | **Cassilda's Song.** You can't stop humming the song, and its lines slip into your speech. You have Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, and any creature that has read the play knows your location while it is within 120 feet of you.                                                                         |
|  **4**  | **The Pallid Mask.** Your face doesn't feel like your own, and you keep touching it. You have Disadvantage on Charisma (Deception and Persuasion) checks, but you can cast *Disguise Self* at will, without a spell slot.                                                                                               |
|  **5**  | **The Repairer of Reputations.** You keep a ledger of every slight against you, and your allies are in it. You can't benefit from the Help action, and you won't let anyone else carry your belongings.                                                                                                                 |
|  **6**  | **The Hyades.** Distant voices sing from a sky that isn't there, drowning out the room around you. You have Disadvantage on Constitution saving throws to maintain Concentration, but you can't have the Deafened condition.                                                                                            |
|  **7**  | **Lake of Hali.** Your limbs feel waterlogged and your lungs feel wet. Your Speed is reduced by 10 feet, but you can breathe water and you have a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.                                                                                                                                       |
|  **8**  | **Yhtill's Spires.** You glimpse impossible towers behind the horizon, and heights pull at you. You have Disadvantage on Strength (Athletics) checks, and whenever you're within 10 feet of a drop of 20 feet or more, you must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or move toward its edge using all your movement. |
|  **9**  | **The Watchman.** A puffy, pale-faced figure watches you from just too far away to reach. You sleep poorly and regain only half your spent Hit Dice on a Long Rest, but you can't be Surprised.                                                                                                                         |
| **10**  | **Not Upon Us, O King.** Despair settles on you, and nothing feels like it will help. You can't gain Heroic Inspiration, and you have Disadvantage on Death Saving Throws.                                                                                                                                              |

constrictor_s_armband.name: Constrictor's Armband
constrictor_s_armband.desc:
While wearing this armband, a creature that's grappled by you suffers a −1d4 penalty to any ability check or saving throw it makes to escape your grapple; the target also takes bludgeoning damage equal to the number rolled on the d4. If the creature rolls a 4 on the d4, it is unable to speak until it is no longer grappled, as it struggles to breathe in your grasp.

*"Turns out, the finest erudition and the most intricate magical words can't do much against a chokehold. Get that one into that big head of yours for next time, eh? And maybe don't struggle so much like a caught fish."
—Bertold the Boa, winner of the DXIV Mage Duels; disqualified because casting misty step once then choking the opponent out was ruled counter to the spirit of the competition*
